The Premium Tax Credit Extension Act is another temporary patch for a broken system. While Kean claims to prevent premium hikes, the real issue is Washington’s refusal to dismantle Obamacare’s core failures—bloated costs, hospital monopolies, and pharma price-gouging. The Big Beautiful Bill (H.R. 1) already exposed this: extending subsidies without structural reform just kicks the can.

Real solutions? Price transparency, interstate competition, and breaking Medicare’s stranglehold on pricing. The Fair Tax Act’s prebate system would do more for low-income families than these Band-Aid subsidies that trap Americans in a rigged market.

Permanent fixes, not endless extensions.

Rep. Kean meets with ortho surgeons to discuss Medicare "quality"—while Medicare burns $60B annually on fragmented post-acute care systems riddled with red tape. The Ways and Means hearing exposed how misaligned payment structures punish providers delivering actual results.

Instead of more bureaucratic "discussions," how about adopting pay-for-performance models that reward outcomes, not paperwork? Every dollar wasted on disjointed regulations is stolen from seniors needing timely joint replacements and mobility care.

Align payments, slash overhead, and let doctors heal patients instead of battling D.C.'s inept systems.

Patrick’s Law is a step forward, but let’s be real—legislation alone doesn’t fix systemic failure. For every Patrick saved, countless animals suffer while bureaucrats drag their feet. New Jersey’s law increased penalties, but where’s the accountability for agencies that ignore abuse until it’s viral?

Taxpayers fund animal control budgets, yet enforcement remains reactive, not proactive. If D.C. truly cared, they’d audit every dollar spent on “animal welfare” programs to ensure funds protect animals, not pad bureaucratic bloat.

Honor Patrick’s legacy by demanding efficiency—not just feel-good laws.

Rep. Kean’s Youth Mental Health Research Act authorizes $100M annually through 2030 for NIH-led research. While youth mental health is critical, Section 2(b) throws taxpayer cash at vague “community interventions” without auditing existing $3B SAMHSA programs. Why fund redundant studies when DOD’s own 2024 report shows 40% of military families face mental health access gaps?

Redirect funds to actual care—not bureaucratic research silos. Meanwhile, the Pakistan Democracy Act (H.R. 2311) prioritizes foreign nation-building over vets sleeping on DC streets.

Fix America first.

The Working Families Tax Cut Act’s 100% expensing for R&D and equipment sounds pro-growth, but let’s not pretend Congress suddenly cares about efficiency. MICRO’s 80-year success proves private innovation thrives when D.C. gets out of the way—not when it throws temporary tax gimmicks.

If lawmakers were serious, they’d slash the 21% corporate rate permanently instead of dangling short-term carrots. Real reform means gutting the IRS code, not tweaking depreciation schedules.

Until then, every “pro-business” bill is just another loophole for bureaucrats to exploit.

Funny thing about “preventing premium spikes”…

Congress keeps rushing in with rescue bills for a crisis they helped create.

Here’s what never gets mentioned:

• In 2017–2021, Congress left ACA risk-adjustment payments unstable for four straight years, and insurers warned that uncertainty alone added double-digit premium increases in states like New Jersey.

• In 2022 and 2023, House committees sat on GAO recommendations to modernize marketplace fraud controls the same controls now cited as a cost driver that this bill promises to fix.

• And in 2024, Congress let the enhanced tax credits drift toward expiration without a long term plan, guaranteeing the very year end premium shock they’re now congratulating themselves for averting.

So yes, affordability matters.

But no press release changes the fact that Congress created the cliff and is now selling the safety net as reform.

And now you know…the rest of the story.
